keepsakes.name: A brass thimble, sea-smoothed
keepsakes.found: Down among the salvage, small and deliberate as a full stop: a brass thimble, kitchen-worn, polished bright by nineteen years of patient water.
keepsakes.hint: Kitchen brass, needle-marked. Somebody at the Brinehouse would know work like this.

keepsakes.name: A bosun's whistle on a green chain
keepsakes.found: Caught in the netting, a bosun's whistle, its chain corroded green, its tone, when you dare one soft note, impossibly clear.
keepsakes.hint: Deck gear, old pattern, crew-issued. The harbormaster's office keeps the crew lists.

keepsakes.name: A championship medal on a rotted ribbon
keepsakes.found: Wedged behind the wreck, where the sea files things: a medal, gold under the tarnish, and a name under the gold. B. MOLENAAR.
keepsakes.hint: The engraving still reads. So will the man by the window.

keepsakes.name: A letter in oilskin, stamped and unsent
keepsakes.found: An oilskin packet, sealed with care by somebody who meant it: a letter, stamped for the coastal mail, never delivered. The address is a chandlery.
keepsakes.hint: Twenty years late is still post. The chandlery is still there.

keepsakes.name: A school slate, ruled for tides
keepsakes.found: In a wax-cloth wrap the water plainly respected: a school slate, chalk ruled into careful columns, the heading still legible. TIDE JOURNAL. KEEP PROPERLY.
keepsakes.hint: You know exactly one committee that would want this back.

keepsakes.name: A wedding band, twice engraved
keepsakes.found: Alone in a salt-fused strongbox, a wedding band of worked gold, engraved inside twice over: E.A., and T.O., and squeezed between them, AND THE MARROWS.
keepsakes.hint: Initials are an address, if you know an archivist.
